tools.name: zurvan_search
tools.title: Search Zurvan memory
tools.description:
Search the Zurvan knowledge base and return ranked matches.

    Use this first to orient yourself on any topic before answering or editing.
    Returns a numbered list of matching wiki pages, each with a relevance score
    and (in hybrid mode) the matched heading plus a short text snippet, so you
    can judge relevance without opening every file.

hybrid.description: Blend FTS5 keyword scoring with local embeddings (best for conceptual queries). False = pure keyword scan.
hybrid.title: Hybrid

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return.
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: zurvan_orient
tools.title: Orient on a topic
tools.description:
One call instead of three: index freshness, hybrid search, and the opening of the top pages.

    Returns the "Search index:" freshness line, the same numbered results as
    zurvan_search, then the first 2,000 characters of each of the top three
    distinct result pages. Use it to start on a topic; continue a page with
    zurvan_read_page and the offset its header names.

tools.name: zurvan_context
tools.title: Build a context bundle
tools.description:
Build a ready-to-read Markdown context bundle for a topic.

    Higher-level than zurvan_search: it gathers the top matches AND (when
    graph=True) their graph neighbours into a single Markdown digest you can
    read in one shot. Use this when you need to understand the decisions,
    claims, and related concepts around a topic before making a change.

topic.description: The subject to assemble context for.
topic.title: Topic

graph.description: Also pull in linked graph neighbours of the top hits.
graph.title: Graph

tools.name: zurvan_read_page
tools.title: Read a knowledge-base page
tools.description:
Read one knowledge-base file, in slices when it is large.

    Use after zurvan_search to open only the page(s) you actually need instead
    of pulling a large context bundle. Returns the raw Markdown (including
    frontmatter). A file bigger than one slice is NOT refused: the result names
    the offset to pass back to read the next part. On unsafe or missing paths it
    returns an actionable error string rather than raising.

path.description: Repo-relative file path (e.g. "wiki/decisions/foo.md" or "docs/API.md"). No absolute paths, no "../"; raw/ is blocked unless ZURVAN_MCP_ALLOW_RAW_READ=1.
path.title: Path

offset.description: Character offset to start reading from. Use the offset the previous call reported to continue a large file.
offset.title: Offset

limit.description: Maximum characters to return in this slice.
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: zurvan_graph_stats
tools.title: Graph size
tools.description:
Return the knowledge graph size as structured {nodes, edges} counts.

    Use as a quick health/size check of the graph before relying on graph tools.
    Emits machine-readable structured output (plus a JSON text fallback).

outputSchema.description: Structured node/edge counts for the knowledge graph.
outputSchema.title: GraphStats

tools.name: zurvan_graph_neighbours
tools.title: Graph neighbours
tools.description:
List one page of a node's direct (one-hop) graph neighbours.

    Use after a search to see what a specific page links to or is linked from
    (decisions, claims, concepts, sources). For multi-hop expansion use
    zurvan_graph_expand instead.

    Results are PAGED: hub nodes in this graph have thousands of edges, and
    returning them all is a single result larger than most context windows. The
    first line reports the range and total, and names the cursor for the rest.

path_or_node_id.description: A wiki path (e.g. "wiki/decisions/foo.md") or a node id.
path_or_node_id.title: Path Or Node Id

limit.description: Maximum neighbours to return in this page.
limit.title: Limit

cursor.description: Offset to resume from; the previous result names the next cursor when more remain.
cursor.title: Cursor

tools.name: zurvan_graph_expand
tools.title: Expand graph neighbourhood
tools.description:
Expand the graph around a node up to `depth` hops, one page at a time.

    Use to discover nearby concepts and notes when building a comprehensive
    picture. Each line is annotated with its hop distance, node type, and the
    relation that connected it.

    Results are ordered NEAREST-FIRST and PAGED, so a first page is the most
    relevant part of the neighbourhood rather than an arbitrary slice.

path_or_node_id.description: A wiki path or node id to expand from.
path_or_node_id.title: Path Or Node Id

depth.description: Number of hops to traverse outward.
depth.title: Depth

limit.description: Maximum entries to return in this page.
limit.title: Limit

cursor.description: Offset to resume from; the previous result names the next cursor when more remain.
cursor.title: Cursor

tools.name: zurvan_status
tools.title: Zurvan status
tools.description:
Report corpus size, search-index freshness, and graph size.

    Call this FIRST in a session. It answers the question every other tool
    depends on: is the index current? A STALE index means search is answering
    from out-of-date content, and a `mock` embedding provider means semantic
    search is meaningless. Also reports whether write tools are enabled.

tools.name: zurvan_eval_search
tools.title: Evaluate retrieval
tools.description:
Run the retrieval-quality evaluation against the gold question set.

    Use to confirm search is healthy after reindexing or large wiki changes.
    Reports top-1/top-3 accuracy and mean reciprocal rank. Read-only and safe.

hybrid.description: Evaluate the hybrid retriever (vs. pure keyword).
hybrid.title: Hybrid

min_top3.description: Minimum acceptable top-3 accuracy; the report flags a failure below this.
min_top3.title: Min Top3

max_queries.description: Run only the first N gold queries. For a LIVENESS check — the full set is the only valid quality measurement.
max_queries.title: Max Queries

tools.name: zurvan_validate_gold
tools.title: Validate gold set
tools.description:
Validate that every path referenced by the gold question set still exists.

    Use to catch a stale evaluation set after files are renamed or removed.
    Read-only and safe.

tools.name: zurvan_remember
tools.title: Record a note
tools.description:
Store a free-form project note in Zurvan memory for future agents.

    Use for general observations that do not fit the structured node kinds. For
    those, prefer the dedicated tools: zurvan_decision_add (architectural
    choices), zurvan_claim_add (evidence-backed facts), zurvan_question_add
    (open questions). Requires write mode (ZURVAN_MCP_READONLY=0).

type.description: Category label for the note; preserved as its first tag.
type.title: Type

tags.description: Topical tags to aid later retrieval.
tags.title: Tags

tools.name: zurvan_decision_add
tools.title: Record a decision
tools.description:
Record an architectural/engineering decision (ADR-style) in Zurvan.

    Use whenever a non-trivial choice is made so future agents respect it.
    Name the subject with `project`. Requires write mode (ZURVAN_MCP_READONLY=0).

title.description: The decision, stated as an outcome (e.g. "Use SQLite FTS5 for search").
title.title: Title

reason.description: The rationale and any considered alternatives.
reason.title: Reason

project.description: The decision's SUBJECT project slug (lowercase letters, digits, '-', '_'), e.g. "acme". Written to the page's `project:` field, which gates publication. Omit only when the server runs inside that project's registered directory; otherwise it is stamped "unknown".
project.title: Project

tools.name: zurvan_decision_set_project
tools.title: Set a decision's project
tools.description:
Correct the `project:` subject of existing decisions INSIDE the ledger.

    Use this, never a direct file edit, when a decision was stamped "unknown" or
    with the wrong project. The slug is validated; only the frontmatter line
    changes; one call is one ledger revision. Requires write mode.

pages.description: Paths of decision pages under wiki/decisions.
pages.title: Pages

project.description: The subject project slug to set, e.g. "acme".
project.title: Project

tools.name: zurvan_decision_supersede
tools.title: Supersede a decision
tools.description:
Link an older decision as superseded by a newer one, INSIDE the ledger.

    The old page gets `status: superseded` and `superseded_by:`, the new one
    `supersedes:`; a superseded decision leaves the recall digest but stays
    searchable. Refused (nothing written) when either decision is not current.
    One call is one ledger revision. Requires write mode.

old.description: The decision being replaced: a page path under wiki/decisions or its slug.
old.title: Old

new.description: The decision that replaces it: a page path or slug.
new.title: New

reason.description: Why the old decision no longer holds.
reason.title: Reason

tools.name: zurvan_claim_add
tools.title: Record an evidenced claim
tools.description:
Record an evidence-backed claim, anchored to a source file.

    The `evidence` text MUST appear verbatim in the `source` file or the claim
    is rejected (no fabricated citations). `source` must be a safe repo-relative
    path. Requires write mode (ZURVAN_MCP_READONLY=0).

source.description: Repo-relative path to the supporting file (no absolute paths, no "../", no raw/ unless ZURVAN_MCP_ALLOW_RAW_READ=1).
source.title: Source

evidence.description: An exact quote from the source file that supports the claim (must appear verbatim).
evidence.title: Evidence

confidence.description: How strongly the evidence supports the claim.
confidence.title: Confidence

tools.name: zurvan_claim_supersede
tools.title: Supersede a claim
tools.description:
Replace a claim with a newer one. The old claim keeps its history, ends
    its validity at `valid_from`, and leaves search and context. Requires write mode.

source.description: Repo-relative path to the supporting file (same rules as zurvan_claim_add).
source.title: Source

evidence.description: An exact quote from the source that supports the newer claim.
evidence.title: Evidence

reason.description: Why the old claim is replaced (required).
reason.title: Reason

valid_from.description: When the newer claim became true (ISO date), if known.
valid_from.title: Valid From

expected_rev.description: The old claim's revision you read; refused CLAIM_CONFLICT if it moved.
expected_rev.title: Expected Rev

tools.name: zurvan_claim_retract
tools.title: Retract a claim
tools.description:
Withdraw a claim. It stays in history and leaves search and context.
    Requires write mode.

basis.description: Basis vocabulary: primary_source, independent_confirmation, direct_measurement, agent_inference, user_assertion.
basis.title: Basis

expected_rev.description: The revision you read; refused CLAIM_CONFLICT if it moved.
expected_rev.title: Expected Rev

tools.name: zurvan_claim_show
tools.title: Show a claim (optionally as of a past revision or date)
tools.description: A claim's state as JSON: now, or as Zurvan believed it at a revision/date.

as_of_revision.description: What Zurvan believed at this knowledge revision.
as_of_revision.title: As Of Revision

as_of_date.description: What Zurvan believed at this ISO date-time.
as_of_date.title: As Of Date

valid_at.description: Keep the claim only if true in the world at this ISO date.
valid_at.title: Valid At

tools.name: zurvan_claim_history
tools.title: Claim history
tools.description: Every revision of a claim as JSON: event, status, actor, method, reason.

tools.name: zurvan_question_add
tools.title: Record an open question
tools.description:
Record an open question / unknown for later investigation.

    Use to capture gaps surfaced during research or editing. Requires write
    mode (ZURVAN_MCP_READONLY=0).

reason.description: Why it matters / what is blocked on it.
reason.title: Reason
